pl-1VXO.title: Landscape: orchards in the south-east
pl-1VXO.summary: Orchards are concentrated around two towns in the south-east.

pl-1Vb3.title: Plants: roads lined with rows of trees
pl-1Vb3.summary: Many roads have a row of trees along each side.

pl-4nMB.title: Chevron: white with red arrows
pl-4nMB.summary: Curve chevrons are white with red arrows.

pl-6stB.title: Sign: green or white-black town entry signs
pl-6stB.summary: Two town entry signs: a green one with the town name, and a white-and-black one with a stylised built-up area. Both use the distinct font.

pl-8spo.title: Language: Ł, Ż, Ń and lots of W
pl-8spo.summary: Slavic language with Ł (stroked L), Ż (dotted Z), Ń, and hooked Ą and Ę. No V, but lots of W, plus many consonant clusters. Ś and Ź also appear in Montenegrin.

pl-E5c9.title: Religion: roadside shrines, Catholic flags
pl-E5c9.summary: A very Catholic country, so roadside Christian shrines are common. Blue-white and yellow-white Catholic flags also appear.

pl-EKCR.title: Sidewalks: neat grey or red tiles
pl-EKCR.summary: Neatly tiled sidewalks are very common, usually grey or light red, in many patterns. Sometimes even roads are tiled.

pl-EruS.title: Street sign: mostly black, blue bottom
pl-EruS.summary: Street signs in this western city are mainly black, with the district in a blue strip at the bottom.

pl-ILmx.title: Pole: yellow markings in west and south
pl-ILmx.summary: Electricity poles with yellow markings are mostly in the west and south.

pl-JBtU.title: Road: coastal forest road with a railway
pl-JBtU.summary: A narrow peninsula's main road runs through coastal forest with a railway track right beside it.

pl-LU2Z.title: Google car: white Gen 4, rare
pl-LU2Z.summary: A white Gen 4 car turns up rarely. It also exists in other European countries, so it is no strong clue.

pl-LdxT.title: Sign: yellow warning triangle, thin red border
pl-LdxT.summary: Warning triangles have a yellow background and a thin red border. In Europe this combination is unique.

pl-OH23.title: Road numbers: 3-digit number tells region
pl-OH23.summary: Regional roads have 3-digit numbers, often in yellow boxes on direction signs. The first digit usually points to a region. This does not work for 2-digit roads.

pl-Pahm.title: Sign: round, white, thick red border
pl-Pahm.summary: Prohibition signs are round with a white background and a thicker red border.

pl-PuJB.title: Pole: black markings, south-east and north
pl-PuJB.summary: Black pole markings are most common in the south-east, plus some parts of the north.

pl-QKpM.title: Houses: Dutch-style old town on the north coast
pl-QKpM.summary: A big northern port city with historic buildings inspired by Dutch Golden Age architecture, a bit like Amsterdam.

pl-QRyL.title: Pole: lamp on the side, rare in north-east
pl-QRyL.summary: Lamps attached to the side of the pole are rarely seen in the north-east.

pl-QpLU.title: Pole: markings on white background, north-east
pl-QpLU.summary: Markings on a white background are most common in the north-east, and occasionally appear in the centre.

pl-RD4g.title: Landscape: very hilly southern border
pl-RD4g.summary: The south has by far the most elevation, with hills and some real mountains, unlike the flat rest of the country.

pl-WkuT.title: Sign: green direction signs, distinct font
pl-WkuT.summary: Normal direction signs are green and use a distinctive font. Expressway signs are blue.

pl-ZbOn.title: Pole: street lamp on top, north-east
pl-ZbOn.summary: Lamps mounted on top of the pole get more common toward the north-east, with a few pockets in the far south.

pl-blym.title: Street sign: green and blue, district at bottom
pl-blym.summary: Street signs in this north-western port city are colourful green and blue with the district at the bottom.

pl-dcsB.title: Place names: -owo north, -ów south
pl-dcsB.summary: Town names ending in -owo are mostly in the northern half, -ów in the southern half. -ino or -yno is mostly northwest and -ew near the centre.

pl-doge.title: Pole: thin concrete with see-through holes
pl-doge.summary: Thin concrete poles with holes through them, known as holey poles. The holes often stop short of the bottom. Hungary and Romania have wider, bulkier ones.

differs.how: Wider, bulkier poles, holes run to the bottom
Wider, bulkier poles, holes run to the bottom

pl-dx99.title: Landscape: tallest mountains on the southern border
pl-dx99.summary: The highest mountains of the country, the Tatras, lie on the southern border with Slovakia.

differs.how: Slovakia's side has the same mountains

pl-gOOw.title: Landscape: flat, green, farmland
pl-gOOw.summary: Mostly flat with some rolling hills, very green, lots of farmland and some forest. Mountains only near the southern border.

pl-gxrJ.title: Signs: rare bilingual signs in some regions
pl-gxrJ.summary: Rare bilingual signs: Kashubian (lots of umlauts) in the north, German near the southwest, Lithuanian and Belarusian near those borders, and Cyrillic Lemko in the southeast.

pl-hZvJ.title: Phone numbers: 9 digits, area code first
pl-hZvJ.summary: Landlines have 9 digits and start with a 2-digit area code that follows regions across the country. Even the first digit narrows the region. Mobile numbers never overlap with landline prefixes.

pl-htL5.title: Sign: pedestrian crossing with one line
pl-htL5.summary: The pedestrian sign shows a single horizontal line instead of zebra stripes. Austria and Belgium use two lines.

pl-k6sd.title: Houses: traditional wooden houses in the east
pl-k6sd.summary: Traditional wooden houses are common in the east, mostly in the north-east.

pl-kRKi.title: Houses: pastel stucco, tidy orange roofs
pl-kRKi.summary: Plain walls covered in light or pastel plaster, with orange, red, black or brown tidy roofs. Detached family homes are common, sometimes blocky. Some rural roofs are corrugated sheet.

pl-lm-3000.title: Sign: single continuous pedestrian line
pl-lm-3000.summary: Horizontal-line pedestrian signs exist in several countries. A single continuous line is found only here.

pl-lm-740366.title: Street sign: blue with metal border and gap
pl-lm-740366.summary: Blue street signs in a metal frame, with a visible gap between the sign and the frame.

pl-lm-740369.title: Street sign: white inner frame, corner dots
pl-lm-740369.summary: Street signs with a white frame inside and white dots in the corners.

pl-mshS.title: Guardrail: normal B-type, round red reflectors
pl-mshS.summary: Standard square-profile (B-type) guardrails with round red reflectors. Very few European countries have this type.

pl-oHYD.title: Road lines: all white, often double middle
pl-oHYD.summary: All-white road lines, and double middle lines are very common here. Denmark and Greece can also have double middle lines.

differs.how: Denmark can also have double middle lines
Greece can also have double middle lines

pl-rudj.title: Google car: black Gen 4, rare
pl-rudj.summary: A black Gen 4 car turns up rarely. It also exists in many other European countries, so it is no strong clue.

pl-v82S.title: Street sign: turquoise, district at bottom
pl-v82S.summary: Street signs in this north-eastern city are turquoise with the district shown at the bottom.

pl-vySo.title: Bollard: red band all the way round
pl-vySo.summary: A white post with a red band wrapping around it, a red reflector on the front and a white one on the back. Sometimes numbered. The same design appears in western Ukraine.

pl-y2jz.title: Plate: long white, blue strip on left
pl-y2jz.summary: Long white plates with the standard European blue strip on the left. Newer electric vehicles have green plates.
